prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this Brackett THE CRESCENTS concept with TWO owner-requested changes. Preserve the image framing, nearly overhead camera, blue-hour stylized 3D art, lilac district boundary, coast and harbour outline, blue/plum domestic roofs, triangular corner shop, existing central-left cul-de-sac and all surrounding streets. CHANGE 1: In the LARGE DENSE HOUSING POCKET ON THE RIGHT, add one clearly legible residential CUL-DE-SAC. Connect its single entrance to the SOUTHERN CURVING PERIMETER STREET of that housing pocket. Run a short narrow access street northward into the middle of the housing group and terminate it with a modest ROUND TURNING HEAD surrounded by front-facing houses and low garden walls. It must be a dead end with ONE road entrance, not a loop, roundabout with exits or through road. Remove or reposition a few existing interior houses and garden plots to give it real visual space; retain varied detached and paired homes around it. A pedestrian-only gap can continue from the turning head through the northern gardens. Do not add a road elsewhere or touch the old central-left cul-de-sac. CHANGE 2: Add a CONTINUOUS COASTAL BOARDWALK following the OUTER SEA EDGE visible down the far LEFT, around the southwest coastal homes, and along the bottom edge toward the next district. This is a narrow public walking promenade, roughly 3-4m visual width, with restrained weathered warm-brown timber decking, broad simple plank seams, low dark metal seaward railing, quiet dark support/fascia, occasional warm lamps. Trace the existing seawall/shore, using edge supports where tight without filling the sea or changing coastline. Retain shore stone/rock below it. The boardwalk continues out of frame north and southeast to imply one consistent shared route around the island. A couple of short landward connections meet existing footpaths; no new vehicular junction. Keep it visibly separated from the road, and open for walking without ornamental clutter. This is not a marina pontoon, no boats or piers and no timber ring around the interior harbour. Preserve all other composition and lighting as closely as possible; neighbourhood outside selected district remains subdued. Road surface detailing is not the focus. No text, labels, watermark or added props unrelated to these changes.
